title: A prime minimal over an associated prime plus (x) is associated to M/x^nM for some n
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] (a Noetherian commutative ring with exactly one maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$) and let $M$ be a finite $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. An *associated prime* of an $R$-module $N$ is a prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset R$ for which there is an element $z\in N$ with $\operatorname{Ann}_R(z):=\{a\in R: az=0\}=\mathfrak p$; $\operatorname{Ass}_R(N)$ is the set of them. Let $x\in\mathfrak m$, let $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Ass}_R(M)$, and let $\mathfrak q$ be a prime ideal of $R$ that is minimal over the ideal $\mathfrak p+(x)$ (that is, $\mathfrak p+(x)\subseteq\mathfrak q$ and no prime ideal $\mathfrak q'$ satisfies $\mathfrak p+(x)\subseteq\mathfrak q'\subsetneq\mathfrak q$). Then there is an integer $n\ge1$ with $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Ass}_R(M/x^nM)$, i.e. some $w\in M/x^nM$ has $\operatorname{Ann}_R(w)=\mathfrak q$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0CN5 (lemma-inherit-minimal-primes, line 17961); associated primes as in Definition Tag 00LA (definition-associated, line 15108)

proof.text: (A copy of $R/\mathfrak p$ in $M$.) Since $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Ass}_R(M)$ there is $z\in M$ with $\operatorname{Ann}_R(z)=\mathfrak p$. Let $N=Rz\subseteq M$. The $R$-linear map $R\to N$, $a\mapsto az$, is surjective with kernel $\operatorname{Ann}_R(z)=\mathfrak p$, so it induces an isomorphism $R/\mathfrak p\cong N$, $\bar a\mapsto az$. In particular $\mathfrak pN=0$, and under this isomorphism $xN=Rxz$ corresponds to $(\mathfrak p+(x))/\mathfrak p$, so $N/xN\cong R/(\mathfrak p+(x))$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 0CN5 (line 17968): 'Pick a submodule N ⊂ M with N ≅ R/p'

proof.text: (Choice of $n$ by Artin–Rees.) Apply [lem-weil-pbc-artin-rees] to the Noetherian ring $R$, the ideal $I=(x)$, the finite $R$-module $M$ and its submodule $N$: there is an integer $c\ge0$ with $I^kM\cap N\subseteq I^{k-c}N$ for all $k\ge c$. Put $n=c+1\ge1$. Since $I^n=(x^n)$ we have $I^nM=x^nM$, and $I^{n-c}N=xN$; hence $N\cap x^nM\subseteq xN$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 0CN5 (line 17969-17970): 'By the Artin-Rees lemma (Lemma 00IN) we can pick n > 0 such that N ∩ x^nM ⊂ xN'

proof.text: (Reduction to $\overline N$.) Let $\pi:M\to M/x^nM$ be the quotient map and $\overline N=\pi(N)\subseteq M/x^nM$, an $R$-submodule, generated by $\bar z=\pi(z)$, hence a finite $R$-module; $\pi$ restricts to a surjection $N\to\overline N$ with kernel $N\cap x^nM$, so $\overline N\cong N/(N\cap x^nM)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-associated-prime-submodule] applied to the Noetherian ring $R$ and the submodule $\overline N$ of $M/x^nM$, $\operatorname{Ass}_R(\overline N)\subseteq\operatorname{Ass}_R(M/x^nM)$; so it suffices to show $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Ass}_R(\overline N)$, i.e. some $w\in\overline N$ has $\operatorname{Ann}_R(w)=\mathfrak q$ (the same $w$ then lies in $M/x^nM$ with the same annihilator).

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 0CN5 (line 17971-17973), citing Lemma Tag 02M3 (lemma-ass)

proof.text: ($\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Supp}(\overline N)$.) Since $N\cap x^nM\subseteq xN$ (Step 2), the surjection $N\to N/xN$ factors through $N/(N\cap x^nM)\cong\overline N$, giving a surjection $\overline N\to N/xN\cong R/(\mathfrak p+(x))$ (Step 1). An element of $R$ killing $\overline N$ kills its quotient $R/(\mathfrak p+(x))$, hence lies in $\mathfrak p+(x)$ (it kills the class of $1$); so $\operatorname{Ann}_R(\overline N)\subseteq\mathfrak p+(x)\subseteq\mathfrak q$. As $\overline N$ is finite (Step 3), [lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-support-annihilator] gives $\overline N_{\mathfrak q}\neq0$, i.e. $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Supp}(\overline N)$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 0CN5 (line 17974-17976): 'there is a surjection N̄ → N/xN = R/p + (x) and hence q is in the support of N̄'

proof.text: ($\mathfrak q$ is minimal in $\operatorname{Supp}(\overline N)$.) $\overline N$ is annihilated by $\mathfrak p$ (since $\mathfrak pN=0$, Step 1, and $\overline N=\pi(N)$) and by $x^n$ (since $x^n(M/x^nM)=0$); so $\mathfrak p+(x^n)\subseteq\operatorname{Ann}_R(\overline N)$. Let $\mathfrak q'\in\operatorname{Supp}(\overline N)$ with $\mathfrak q'\subseteq\mathfrak q$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-support-annihilator] ($\overline N$ finite), $\operatorname{Ann}_R(\overline N)\subseteq\mathfrak q'$, so $\mathfrak p\subseteq\mathfrak q'$ and $x^n\in\mathfrak q'$, hence $x\in\mathfrak q'$ as $\mathfrak q'$ is prime. Thus $\mathfrak p+(x)\subseteq\mathfrak q'\subseteq\mathfrak q$, and $\mathfrak q'=\mathfrak q$ by the minimality of $\mathfrak q$ over $\mathfrak p+(x)$. So $\mathfrak q$ is a minimal element of $\operatorname{Supp}(\overline N)$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 0CN5 (line 17977-17978): 'Since N̄ is annihilated by x^n and p we see that q is minimal among the primes in the support of N̄'

proof.text: (Conclusion.) By [lem-weil-pbc-minimal-support-prime-associated] applied to the Noetherian ring $R$ and the finite $R$-module $\overline N$ (Step 3), with $\mathfrak q$ minimal in $\operatorname{Supp}(\overline N)$ (Steps 4 and 5), there is $w\in\overline N$ with $\operatorname{Ann}_R(w)=\mathfrak q$. By Step 3, $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Ass}_R(M/x^nM)$ with $n=c+1\ge1$.
